questions.explanation: The Atacama occupies a coastal strip of northern Chile in the Andean rain shadow.

questions.question: The Gobi Desert spans parts of which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Gobi covers southern Mongolia and northern China.

questions.question: The Kalahari Desert covers much of which country?
questions.explanation: The semi-arid Kalahari covers most of Botswana, extending into Namibia and South Africa.

questions.question: The Namib Desert, famous for towering red dunes, lies along the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Namib runs along the Atlantic coast of Namibia and is one of the world's oldest deserts.

questions.question: The Thar Desert straddles the border between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Thar (Great Indian Desert) lies across the India-Pakistan frontier, mostly in Rajasthan and Sindh.

questions.question: The Taklamakan Desert, one of the largest sandy deserts in the world, lies within which country?
questions.explanation: The Taklamakan fills the Tarim Basin in the Xinjiang region of China.

questions.question: The Patagonian Desert, the largest desert in the Americas, lies mostly within which country?
questions.explanation: The Patagonian Desert covers a large part of southern Argentina east of the Andes.

questions.question: What is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea, an endorheic salt lake, is the largest inland body of water by surface area.

questions.question: Which lake is the deepest in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches about 1,642 m deep, the deepest lake on Earth.

questions.question: What is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior covers about 82,100 square kilometres, the largest freshwater lake by area, while Baikal holds the most freshwater by volume.

questions.question: Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world, straddles the border of Peru and which country?
questions.explanation: Titicaca sits at about 3,812 m on the Peru-Bolivia border in the Andes.

questions.question: Besides Tanzania and Uganda, which country borders Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is bordered by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.

questions.question: The shrinking Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Aral Sea straddles the border of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

questions.question: Which country does NOT border Lake Tanganyika?
questions.explanation: Lake Tanganyika is bordered by Tanzania, DR Congo, Burundi and Zambia, but not Kenya.

questions.question: Which of the North American Great Lakes lies entirely within the United States?
questions.explanation: Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake wholly within the United States; the others are shared with Canada.

questions.question: Besides Chad, Cameroon and Nigeria, which country borders Lake Chad?
questions.explanation: Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Cameroon, Nigeria and Niger.

questions.question: The active volcanoes Mauna Loa and Kilauea are located on which island?
questions.explanation: Both Mauna Loa and Kilauea are on Hawaii's Big Island.

questions.question: Mount Vesuvius, which destroyed Pompeii in AD 79, overlooks which Italian city?
questions.explanation: Vesuvius rises over the Bay of Naples in southern Italy.

questions.question: What is the highest volcano in the world?
questions.explanation: Ojos del Salado (about 6,893 m) on the Chile-Argentina border is the highest volcano and Chile's highest peak.

questions.question: The catastrophic 1883 eruption, one of the deadliest and loudest in recorded history, was produced by which volcano?
questions.explanation: Krakatoa, in the Sunda Strait of Indonesia, erupted catastrophically in 1883.

questions.question: Mount Etna, the most active volcano in Europe, is located on which island?
questions.explanation: Etna dominates the east coast of the Italian island of Sicily.

questions.question: The 1991 eruption of which Philippine volcano was the second-largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century?
questions.explanation: Mount Pinatubo's 1991 eruption on Luzon was the century's second-largest, cooling global temperatures.

questions.question: Cotopaxi, one of the world's highest active volcanoes, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Cotopaxi is a snow-capped active volcano in the Andes of Ecuador.

questions.question: Mount Erebus, the southernmost active volcano on Earth, is located on which continent?
questions.explanation: Mount Erebus, on Ross Island, is Antarctica's most active volcano.

questions.question: Eyjafjallajokull, whose 2010 eruption grounded much of Europe's air traffic, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Eyjafjallajokull is a glacier-capped volcano in southern Iceland.

questions.question: The active volcano Popocatepetl looms near which major capital city?
questions.explanation: Popocatepetl lies about 70 km southeast of Mexico City.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean to which sea?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar links the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea between Spain and Morocco.

questions.question: The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and which island?
questions.explanation: This busy shipping strait runs between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

questions.question: The Bosphorus Strait, which divides Istanbul, connects the Black Sea to which sea?
questions.explanation: The Bosphorus links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.

questions.question: The Strait of Hormuz, a key oil chokepoint, connects the Persian Gulf to which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz joins the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

questions.question: The Bering Strait separates Russia from which U.S. state?
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait lies between Russia's Chukchi Peninsula and Alaska.

questions.question: The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait connects the Red Sea to which body of water?
questions.explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.

questions.question: The Strait of Magellan is located near the southern tip of which continent?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Magellan cuts through the southern end of South America.

questions.question: The Dardanelles connects the Sea of Marmara to which sea?
questions.explanation: The Dardanelles links the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea.

questions.question: The Palk Strait separates India from which island nation?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between southeastern India and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: The Cook Strait separates the two main islands of which country?
questions.explanation: Cook Strait separates the North and South Islands of New Zealand.

questions.question: The Strait of Dover, the narrowest part of the English Channel, separates southeastern England from which country?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Dover is the narrowest point of the English Channel, separating England from France by about 33 km.

questions.question: What is the largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland, at about 2.16 million square kilometres, is the world's largest island (Australia is classed as a continent).

questions.question: Which is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Sicily, at about 25,700 square kilometres, is the largest Mediterranean island.

questions.question: The island of Borneo is divided among Indonesia, Malaysia, and which third country?
questions.explanation: Borneo is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and the small sultanate of Brunei.

questions.question: The island of Hispaniola is shared by Haiti and which country?
questions.explanation: Hispaniola is divided between Haiti in the west and the Dominican Republic in the east.

questions.question: Which is the fourth-largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: The order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, then Madagascar as the fourth-largest island.

questions.question: Honshu is the largest island of which country?
questions.explanation: Honshu is Japan's largest and most populous island, home to Tokyo.

questions.question: The island of New Guinea is politically divided between Indonesia and which country?
questions.explanation: The eastern half of New Guinea forms the independent state of Papua New Guinea.

questions.question: Baffin Island, the largest island in Canada, lies within which territory?
questions.explanation: Baffin Island, Canada's largest island, is part of the territory of Nunavut.

questions.question: The Galapagos Islands, famous for their unique wildlife, belong to which country?
questions.explanation: The Galapagos are a province of Ecuador, about 1,000 km off its Pacific coast.

questions.question: Tasmania is an island state of which country?
questions.explanation: Tasmania lies south of the mainland and is a state of Australia.

questions.question: Which sea is unique in having no land coastline, being bounded on all sides by ocean currents?
questions.explanation: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is the only sea defined entirely by surrounding ocean currents (including the Gulf Stream) rather than land boundaries.

questions.question: The Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in Earth's oceans, lies in which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Challenger Deep sits in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean, reaching roughly 10,900 meters below sea level.

questions.question: Which strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, separating the Arabian Peninsula from the Horn of Africa?
questions.explanation: The Bab-el-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden between Yemen and Djibouti/Eritrea.

questions.question: The Bosporus Strait connects the Black Sea to which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Bosporus, running through Istanbul, joins the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, which in turn connects to the Aegean via the Dardanelles.

questions.question: What is the world's largest inland body of water by surface area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea, at about 371,000 km2, is the largest fully enclosed inland body of water on Earth.

questions.question: Excluding enclosed lakes such as the Dead Sea, which is the saltiest open sea connected to the world ocean?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea, with high evaporation and little freshwater inflow, reaches about 40 parts per thousand salinity, the saltiest of the ocean-connected seas.

questions.question: The Sea of Azov is connected to the Black Sea by which strait?
questions.explanation: The Kerch Strait links the shallow Sea of Azov to the Black Sea between the Crimean and Taman peninsulas.

questions.question: The Drake Passage separates the southern tip of South America from which landmass?
questions.explanation: The Drake Passage is the body of water between Cape Horn and the Antarctic Peninsula.

questions.question: The Adriatic Sea connects to the Ionian Sea through which strait?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Otranto, between Italy and Albania, is the passage linking the Adriatic to the Ionian Sea.

questions.question: The Skagerrak and Kattegat straits link the North Sea to which sea?
questions.explanation: The Skagerrak and Kattegat, between Denmark, Norway, and Sweden, form the maritime route connecting the North Sea toward the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: The Dardanelles strait connects the Sea of Marmara to which sea?
questions.explanation: The Dardanelles links the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea, completing the Turkish Straits system.

questions.question: The Gulf of Bothnia, lying between Sweden and Finland, is the northern arm of which sea?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Bothnia is the northernmost extension of the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: Which is the smallest and shallowest of the world's five oceans?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean is by far the smallest and shallowest of the five recognized oceans.

questions.question: Which two countries are tied for sharing land borders with the greatest number of other countries (14 each)?
questions.explanation: Both China and Russia each border 14 sovereign states, more than any other country.

questions.question: The longest international land border between two countries is shared by which pair?
questions.explanation: The Canada-United States border stretches about 8,891 km (including the Alaska-Canada section), the longest between any two nations.

questions.question: Which country is the only one with coastlines on both the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf?
questions.explanation: Iran is the sole country bordering both the Caspian Sea to its north and the Persian Gulf to its south.

questions.question: Which country completely surrounds two independent sovereign states within its territory?
questions.explanation: Italy fully encloses both San Marino and Vatican City.

questions.question: The Gambia is almost entirely surrounded by the territory of which single country?
questions.explanation: The Gambia is enclosed by Senegal on all sides except its short Atlantic coastline.

questions.question: On the island of Borneo, Brunei shares its only land border with which country?
questions.explanation: Brunei's entire land boundary is with the Malaysian state of Sarawak, which also splits Brunei into two parts.

questions.question: Which two countries share the longest international border in South America?
questions.explanation: The Argentina-Chile border, running along the Andes for over 5,000 km, is the longest in South America.

questions.question: Which African country borders nine others, the most of any nation on the continent?
questions.explanation: The Democratic Republic of the Congo borders nine countries, more than any other African state.

questions.question: Brazil shares a land border with every South American country except Chile and which other?
questions.explanation: Chile and Ecuador are the only two South American nations that do not touch Brazil's vast borders.

questions.question: The McMahon Line is a disputed boundary between India and which country?
questions.explanation: The McMahon Line, drawn in 1914, is the disputed frontier between India's Arunachal Pradesh and China.

questions.question: The Durand Line forms the international boundary between Pakistan and which country?
questions.explanation: The Durand Line, established in 1893, marks the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

questions.question: The Radcliffe Line, drawn in 1947, demarcated the partition border between India and the newly created state of what?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line separated British India into India and Pakistan at independence in 1947 (East Pakistan later became Bangladesh).

questions.question: Mongolia is a landlocked country bordered by exactly two nations: Russia and which other?
questions.explanation: Mongolia lies between Russia to the north and China on all other sides.

questions.question: Bhutan shares land borders with only two countries: India and which other?
questions.explanation: Bhutan borders only India to the south and China to the north; it does not touch Nepal.

questions.question: Norway's land borders are with Sweden, Finland, and which third country?
questions.explanation: Norway shares a short northern land border with Russia in addition to Sweden and Finland.

questions.question: Kaliningrad Oblast is an exclave of which country, cut off from its mainland by Lithuania and Poland?
questions.explanation: Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave on the Baltic coast, physically separated from the rest of Russia.

questions.question: The Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic is an exclave of which country, separated from the mainland by Armenia?
questions.explanation: Nakhchivan is an exclave of Azerbaijan, reachable overland only through Iran or Turkey because Armenia lies between it and Azerbaijan proper.

questions.question: The oil-rich exclave of Cabinda, separated from its mainland by the Democratic Republic of the Congo, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Cabinda is a province of Angola detached from the rest of the country by a strip of DRC territory reaching the Atlantic.

questions.question: The town of Busingen am Hochrhein is a German exclave entirely surrounded by which country?
questions.explanation: Busingen is a German municipality completely encircled by Swiss territory.

questions.question: Campione d'Italia is an Italian exclave surrounded by the territory of which country?
questions.explanation: Campione d'Italia sits on Lake Lugano, entirely enclosed by the Swiss canton of Ticino.

questions.question: The Spanish autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla are enclaves bordered by which country?
questions.explanation: Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish enclaves on the North African coast, surrounded by Morocco.

questions.question: Point Roberts, a small exclave of the United States, can only be reached overland by passing through which country?
questions.explanation: Point Roberts hangs below the 49th parallel but is cut off from the rest of Washington State, accessible by land only via Canada.

questions.question: Besides Vatican City, which independent country is an enclave entirely surrounded by Italy?
questions.explanation: San Marino is a fully independent republic completely enclosed by Italian territory.

questions.question: The intricate patchwork of enclaves at Baarle is divided between the Netherlands and which country?
questions.explanation: Baarle-Nassau (Netherlands) and Baarle-Hertog (Belgium) form a famous tangle of Belgian and Dutch enclaves and counter-enclaves.

questions.question: Until a 2015 territorial exchange, the Cooch Behar area contained more than 100 enclaves shared between India and which country?
questions.explanation: India and Bangladesh swapped over 160 enclaves in 2015 to rationalize the tangled Cooch Behar border.

questions.question: The town of Llivia is a Spanish exclave surrounded by the territory of which country?
questions.explanation: Llivia is a Spanish exclave in the Pyrenees, entirely encircled by French territory.

questions.question: Which country is a landlocked enclave entirely surrounded by the territory of South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa, one of only three countries fully enclosed by a single other nation (with Vatican City and San Marino).

questions.question: Which is the largest dependent (non-sovereign) territory in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Greenland, at roughly 2.16 million km2, is by far the largest dependent territory on Earth.

questions.question: The Pacific territory of New Caledonia is a special collectivity of which country?
questions.explanation: New Caledonia is a sui generis collectivity of France in the southwest Pacific.

questions.question: Aruba, Curacao, and Sint Maarten are self-governing constituent countries within the kingdom of which state?
questions.explanation: These Caribbean islands are constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands alongside the Netherlands itself.

questions.question: The Cook Islands and Niue are self-governing states in free association with which country?
questions.explanation: Both the Cook Islands and Niue are in free association with New Zealand, sharing its head of state and citizenship.

questions.question: The autonomous, Swedish-speaking Aland Islands belong to which country?
questions.explanation: The demilitarized, Swedish-speaking Aland Islands are an autonomous region of Finland.

questions.question: The Arctic archipelago of Svalbard is under the sovereignty of which country?
questions.explanation: Svalbard is governed by Norway under the terms of the 1920 Svalbard Treaty.

questions.question: The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory whose sovereignty is also claimed by which country?
questions.explanation: Argentina claims the Falklands (which it calls the Malvinas), a dispute that led to the 1982 war with the United Kingdom.

questions.question: French Guiana, an overseas department of France, is located on which continent?
questions.explanation: French Guiana lies on the northeast coast of South America, making France a continental neighbor of Brazil and Suriname.

questions.question: The Faroe Islands are a self-governing territory of which country?
questions.explanation: The Faroe Islands are an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

questions.question: Which is the southernmost capital city of a sovereign state?
questions.explanation: Wellington, at about 41 degrees S, is the southernmost capital of any sovereign nation.

questions.question: Which is the northernmost capital city of a sovereign state?
questions.explanation: Reykjavik, at roughly 64 degrees N, is the northernmost capital of an independent country.

questions.question: What is the capital city of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Germany?
questions.explanation: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Italy?
questions.explanation: Rome is the capital of Italy.

questions.question: What is the capital city of China?
questions.explanation: Beijing is the capital of China, while Shanghai is its largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital city of India?
questions.explanation: New Delhi is the capital of India.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt.

questions.question: What is the capital city of South Korea?
questions.explanation: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brasília, inaugurated in 1960, is Brazil's capital, not Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Argentina?
questions.explanation: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Norway?
questions.explanation: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Morocco?
questions.explanation: Rabat is Morocco's capital, while Casablanca is its largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Vietnam?
questions.explanation: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam; Ho Chi Minh City is the largest city.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Poland?
questions.explanation: Warsaw is the capital and largest city of Poland.

questions.question: What is the official (constitutional) capital of the Netherlands?
questions.explanation: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital, though the government sits in The Hague.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Pakistan?

questions.question: What is the capital city of Mongolia?

questions.question: What is the capital city of Uzbekistan?

questions.question: What is the capital city of Zimbabwe?

questions.question: What is the capital city of Rwanda?

questions.question: Which continent contains the greatest number of sovereign countries?
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 sovereign states, more than any other continent.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of Earth's land.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest of the continents by land area.

questions.question: Which continent has no permanent human population?
questions.explanation: Antarctica has only temporary research staff and no permanent residents.

questions.question: Which country was formerly known as Ceylon?

questions.question: Which country was historically known as Persia?

questions.question: Which country was formerly known as Siam?

questions.question: Which modern country was formerly known as Rhodesia?

questions.question: Which country, independent since 2011, is the world's most recently created widely recognized sovereign state?

questions.question: The Iberian Peninsula is occupied mainly by Spain and which other country?

questions.question: The Scandinavian Peninsula is shared primarily by Norway and which country?

questions.question: Which is the only country that occupies an entire continent?
questions.explanation: Australia is the only country that is also a continent.

questions.question: The Isthmus of Panama connects North America to which continent?
questions.explanation: Panama forms the land bridge linking North and South America.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in Africa by land area?
questions.explanation: Algeria, at about 2.38 million km², is Africa's largest country by area.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in South America by land area?
questions.explanation: Brazil is by far the largest country in South America.

questions.question: By what earlier name was Ethiopia historically known?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia was long known to outsiders as Abyssinia.

questions.question: Which river is traditionally regarded as the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile, at roughly 6,650 km, is traditionally considered the world's longest river.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine flows through Paris.

questions.question: Which river forms much of the border between the United States and Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Rio Grande marks a long stretch of the Texas–Mexico border.

questions.question: The Ganges River empties into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Ganges drains into the Bay of Bengal via a large delta.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Rome?

questions.question: The Mississippi River empties into which body of water?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi drains into the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.question: The Yellow River (Huang He) flows through which country?
questions.explanation: The Yellow River is the second-longest river in China.

questions.question: The Indus River flows mainly through which present-day country?

questions.question: The Rhine River empties into which sea?
questions.explanation: The Rhine reaches the North Sea through the Netherlands.

questions.question: At Khartoum, the Blue Nile joins which other river to form the main Nile?
questions.explanation: The Blue Nile and White Nile meet at Khartoum, Sudan.

questions.question: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji, at 3,776 m, is Japan's highest peak.

questions.question: The Matterhorn straddles the border between Switzerland and which country?
questions.explanation: The Matterhorn sits on the Swiss–Italian border.

questions.question: Which is the longest mountain range on land (above sea level)?
questions.explanation: The Andes stretch about 7,000 km along western South America.

questions.question: Ben Nevis, the highest peak in the United Kingdom, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis, at 1,345 m, is in the Scottish Highlands.

questions.question: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest peak on the mainland of which country?
questions.explanation: Kosciuszko (2,228 m) is the highest point on the Australian mainland.

questions.question: Aoraki / Mount Cook is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: Aoraki / Mount Cook (3,724 m) is New Zealand's highest peak.

questions.question: Table Mountain overlooks which city?

questions.question: Mount Olympus, the mythological home of the Greek gods, is the highest mountain in which country?

questions.question: The Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter), the world's largest continuous sand desert, lies mainly in which region?

questions.question: The Mojave Desert is located primarily in which country?

questions.question: The largest desert in Australia is the?

questions.question: The Karakum Desert covers much of which country?

questions.question: The Sahel is a semi-arid transition zone lying just south of which desert?

questions.question: The Sonoran Desert straddles the border between the United States and which country?

questions.question: The Danakil Desert, among the hottest regions on Earth, lies mainly in which country?

questions.question: How many oceans are recognized in the modern five-ocean model?

questions.question: Which ocean surrounds the continent of Antarctica?

questions.question: The Dead Sea, whose shore is the lowest exposed land on Earth, borders Jordan, the West Bank, and which country?

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches along Australia's northeastern coast.

questions.question: The Bay of Bengal is bordered to the west by which country?
questions.explanation: India forms the western shore of the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: The Caribbean Sea is part of which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Caribbean Sea is a marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Australia and New Zealand?

questions.question: The Sea of Marmara lies entirely within the territory of which country?

questions.question: Which sea separates the Korean Peninsula from the Japanese archipelago?

questions.question: The Timor Sea separates northern Australia from which island nation?

questions.question: The Gulf Stream is a warm ocean current in which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream flows through the North Atlantic, warming Western Europe.

questions.question: The Bering Sea lies between Alaska and which country?
questions.explanation: The Bering Sea separates Alaska (U.S.) from the Russian Far East.

questions.question: The Ross Sea and Weddell Sea are marginal seas of which ocean?
questions.explanation: Both are large embayments of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica.

questions.question: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands, which lie beside the Andaman Sea, are a territory of which country?
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a union territory of India.

questions.question: Which is the largest gulf in the world by area?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is the world's largest gulf.

questions.question: Portugal shares its only land border with which country?

questions.question: Which two South American countries are landlocked?

questions.question: Which is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia?

questions.question: Nepal is landlocked between India and which other country?
questions.explanation: Nepal lies between India to the south and China to the north.

questions.question: Bolivia lost its Pacific coastline to which country in the 19th-century War of the Pacific?
questions.explanation: Chile annexed Bolivia's coastal region, leaving Bolivia landlocked.

questions.question: The 49th parallel forms much of the border between the United States and which country?
questions.explanation: Much of the U.S.–Canada border follows the 49th parallel.

questions.question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada's deeply indented coastline is the world's longest, over 200,000 km.

questions.question: Ethiopia became landlocked in 1993 after the independence of which neighbor?
questions.explanation: Eritrea's independence in 1993 cut off Ethiopia's access to the Red Sea.

questions.question: Which landlocked Southern African country was formerly called Swaziland?
questions.explanation: Swaziland was renamed Eswatini in 2018.

questions.question: Andorra is a small landlocked country lying between France and which country?
questions.explanation: Andorra sits in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

questions.question: Which country shares a land border with only the United States?
questions.explanation: Canada's only land neighbor is the United States, whereas Mexico also borders Guatemala and Belize.

questions.question: How many countries does Germany share a land border with?
questions.explanation: Germany borders nine countries, among the most of any nation in Europe.

questions.question: Which is the largest landlocked country in Africa by area?
questions.explanation: Chad, at about 1.28 million km², is Africa's largest landlocked country.

questions.question: The demilitarized zone near the 38th parallel divides which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Korean DMZ separates North and South Korea near the 38th parallel.

questions.question: Which is the second-largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: New Guinea is the second-largest island, after Greenland.

questions.question: Which is the third-largest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Borneo ranks third in size, behind Greenland and New Guinea.

questions.question: Which is the largest island in Europe?
questions.explanation: Great Britain is Europe's largest island.

questions.question: Which is the largest island in the Caribbean?
questions.explanation: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean Sea.

questions.question: Corsica is an island belonging to which country?
questions.explanation: Corsica is a territorial collectivity of France.

questions.question: Sardinia is an island belonging to which country?
questions.explanation: Sardinia is an autonomous region of Italy.

questions.question: The Canary Islands are an autonomous region of which country?
questions.explanation: The Canary Islands, off northwest Africa, belong to Spain.

questions.question: Crete is the largest island of which country?
questions.explanation: Crete is the largest and most populous Greek island.

questions.question: Zanzibar is a semi-autonomous archipelago off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Zanzibar lies off Tanzania and forms part of that country.

questions.question: Which is the most populous island in the world?
questions.explanation: Java, in Indonesia, is home to well over 140 million people.

questions.question: Which large island at South America's southern tip is shared by Argentina and Chile?
questions.explanation: Tierra del Fuego is divided between Argentina and Chile.

questions.question: Vancouver Island lies off the west coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Vancouver Island is off the coast of British Columbia, Canada.

questions.question: The Maldives, the world's lowest-lying country, are located in which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Maldives are a chain of atolls in the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Bali, a popular resort island, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Bali is one of Indonesia's provinces.

questions.question: The imaginary line at 0° latitude that circles the Earth is called the?
questions.explanation: The Equator is the line of 0° latitude dividing the hemispheres.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer lies at approximately which latitude?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer sits at about 23.5° north of the Equator.

questions.question: A 'Mediterranean climate' is typically characterized by?
options: Cold dry summers and warm wet winters
Hot dry summers and mild wet winters
questions.explanation: Mediterranean climates feature hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.

questions.question: The cold, treeless biome underlain by permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost) is called the?
questions.explanation: The tundra is defined by permafrost and a lack of trees.

questions.question: Which country takes its name from the Equator that runs through it?
questions.explanation: Ecuador is Spanish for 'equator', which crosses the country.

questions.question: The seasonal wind system that brings a heavy summer rainy season to South Asia is the?
questions.explanation: The summer monsoon brings South Asia's main rains.

questions.question: The vast subarctic coniferous forest spanning Russia and Canada, also called the taiga, is known as the?
questions.explanation: The taiga is also called the boreal forest.

questions.question: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through which city?
questions.explanation: The Prime Meridian is defined through Greenwich in London.

questions.question: What is the largest peninsula in the world?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula, about 3.2 million km², is the world's largest.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in the Middle East by land area?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia is the Middle East's largest country by area.

questions.question: What is the world's largest salt flat, located in Bolivia?
questions.explanation: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat on Earth.

questions.question: Which is the smallest country in South America by land area?
questions.explanation: Suriname is the smallest sovereign state in South America.

questions.question: Measured from its base on the ocean floor to its summit, which is the tallest mountain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Mauna Kea rises about 10,000 m from its Pacific base, exceeding Everest's height above sea level.

questions.question: What is the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is by far the largest tropical rainforest.

questions.question: What does the acronym OPEC stand for?
options: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
Organization for Petroleum and Energy Cooperation
Organization of Petroleum Economies and Companies
questions.explanation: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a cartel that coordinates oil policy among member states.

questions.question: In which city is OPEC headquartered?
questions.explanation: OPEC has been headquartered in Vienna, Austria, since 1965.

questions.question: OPEC was founded in 1960 at a conference held in which city?
questions.explanation: OPEC was established in September 1960 at the Baghdad Conference in Iraq.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation WHO stand for?
questions.explanation: WHO is the World Health Organization, the United Nations' specialized public-health agency.

questions.question: The World Health Organization is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The WHO's headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: In what year was the United Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The United Nations was established in 1945 after World War II, with its Charter taking effect that October.

questions.question: The League of Nations, the forerunner of the United Nations, was created in the aftermath of which war?
questions.explanation: The League of Nations was founded after World War I to promote collective security.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: Alongside Brussels and Strasbourg, which city hosts several EU institutions, including the Court of Justice of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Luxembourg City hosts the Court of Justice of the European Union and other EU bodies.

questions.question: The European Parliament holds its official plenary sessions in which French city?
questions.explanation: The European Parliament's official seat for plenary sessions is Strasbourg, France.

questions.question: What principle is enshrined in Article 5 of the NATO treaty?
options: An armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all
Adoption of a single shared currency
questions.explanation: Article 5 establishes collective defense: an attack on one NATO member is treated as an attack on all.

questions.question: In what year was NATO founded?
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was established in 1949.

questions.question: The African Union is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.question: In the original grouping BRICS, which country does the letter 'S' represent?
questions.explanation: In the original BRICS bloc the 'S' stands for South Africa, which joined the founding four (Brazil, Russia, India, China) in 2010.

questions.question: What does the acronym ASEAN stand for?
options: Asian Sovereign Economic Alliance of Nations
Association of Sovereign East Asian Nations
questions.explanation: ASEAN is the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

questions.question: The ASEAN Secretariat is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat is based in Jakarta, Indonesia.

questions.question: The Commonwealth of Nations is composed largely of former territories of which empire?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth of Nations consists mostly of former parts of the British Empire.

questions.question: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, both created at the 1944 Bretton Woods conference, are headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: Both the IMF and the World Bank have their headquarters in Washington, D.C.

questions.question: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: INTERPOL, the international criminal police organization, is headquartered in which French city?
questions.explanation: INTERPOL's General Secretariat is located in Lyon, France.

questions.question: The G7 includes the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, and Japan. Which country is the seventh member?
questions.explanation: Canada is the seventh member of the G7 group of advanced economies.

questions.question: The Organization of American States (OAS) is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The OAS has its headquarters in Washington, D.C.

questions.question: The Arab League is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The League of Arab States is headquartered in Cairo, Egypt.

questions.question: The UN agency UNESCO is primarily concerned with which fields?
questions.explanation: UNESCO promotes international cooperation in education, science, and culture.

questions.question: How many non-permanent members serve on the UN Security Council at any given time?
questions.explanation: The Security Council has 10 non-permanent members serving alongside its 5 permanent members.

questions.question: The Cold War military alliance known as the Warsaw Pact was led by which country?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Pact was a defense alliance of Eastern Bloc states led by the Soviet Union.

questions.question: What is the official currency of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian rupee is the official currency of India.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Denmark?
questions.explanation: Denmark uses the Danish krone and has not adopted the euro.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Thailand?
questions.explanation: The baht is the official currency of Thailand.

questions.question: What is the official currency of South Korea?
questions.explanation: The South Korean won is the official currency of South Korea.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Israel?
questions.explanation: The Israeli new shekel is the official currency of Israel.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Brazil?
questions.explanation: The real is the official currency of Brazil.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Russia?
questions.explanation: The ruble is the official currency of Russia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Turkey?
questions.explanation: The lira is the official currency of Turkey.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: The riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of South Africa?
questions.explanation: The rand is the official currency of South Africa.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The naira is the official currency of Nigeria.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Egypt?
questions.explanation: The Egyptian pound is the official currency of Egypt.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Switzerland?
questions.explanation: Switzerland uses the Swiss franc.

questions.question: What is the official currency of China?
questions.explanation: China's official currency is the yuan, the base unit of the renminbi.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Indonesia?
questions.explanation: The rupiah is the official currency of Indonesia.

questions.question: What is the official currency of Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The taka is the official currency of Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which South American country abandoned its own currency (the sucre) and adopted the US dollar as legal tender in 2000?
questions.explanation: Ecuador replaced the sucre with the US dollar as its official currency in 2000.

questions.question: In which year did euro banknotes and coins first enter circulation?
questions.explanation: Although the euro launched electronically in 1999, physical notes and coins entered circulation on 1 January 2002.

questions.question: A single red maple leaf is the central emblem on the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Canada's flag features a stylized red maple leaf between two red bands.

questions.question: Which country's national flag consists of a single red circle (a sun disk) on a plain white field?
questions.explanation: Japan's flag depicts a red sun disk centered on a white field.

questions.question: Which country's flag features the Union Jack in the canton, the Southern Cross, and a large seven-pointed Commonwealth Star?
questions.explanation: Australia's flag combines the Union Jack, the Southern Cross, and the seven-pointed Commonwealth Star.

questions.question: The off-center 'Nordic Cross' design appears on the flags of Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, and which other country?
questions.explanation: Iceland's flag uses the Nordic Cross, completing the set of Scandinavian cross flags.

questions.question: The Dannebrog, often cited as the oldest continuously used national flag in the world, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Denmark's Dannebrog is widely regarded as the oldest continuously used national flag.

questions.question: A blue Star of David between two horizontal blue stripes appears on the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Israel's flag features a blue Star of David between two horizontal blue stripes on white.

questions.question: The banner on Brazil's flag reads 'Ordem e Progresso.' What does this motto mean?
questions.explanation: 'Ordem e Progresso' is Portuguese for 'Order and Progress.'

questions.question: The 13 horizontal stripes on the flag of the United States represent what?
options: The 13 amendments in the Bill of Rights
questions.explanation: The 13 stripes symbolize the 13 original British colonies that declared independence.

questions.question: The red-and-blue circle at the center of South Korea's flag is known by what name?
questions.explanation: The central symbol on the South Korean flag is the Taegeuk, representing balance and harmony.

questions.question: The navy-blue 24-spoke wheel at the center of India's national flag is called the:
questions.explanation: The wheel on India's flag is the Ashoka Chakra, a dharma wheel with 24 spokes.

questions.question: A white crescent moon and five-pointed star on a plain red field form the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Turkey's flag is a white crescent and star on a solid red field.

questions.question: Three equal horizontal bands of black, red, and gold form the national flag of which country?
questions.explanation: Germany's flag consists of horizontal black, red, and gold bands.

questions.question: Which country's national flag features a golden bird of paradise and the Southern Cross on a red-and-black field?
questions.explanation: Papua New Guinea's flag depicts a golden bird of paradise alongside the Southern Cross.

questions.question: The Union Jack combines the crosses of Saint George (England), Saint Andrew (Scotland), and Saint Patrick, who represents which country?
questions.explanation: Saint Patrick's saltire on the Union Jack represents Ireland.

questions.question: The national flag of Wales prominently features which creature?
questions.explanation: The Welsh flag depicts a red dragon (Y Ddraig Goch) on a green-and-white field.

questions.question: The national flag of Kenya features a traditional Maasai shield flanked by two crossed:
questions.explanation: Kenya's flag shows a Maasai shield with two crossed spears at its center.

questions.question: The bald eagle is the national bird and a prominent national symbol of which country?
questions.explanation: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States.

questions.question: The flightless kiwi bird is such an iconic national symbol that it has become an informal name for the people of which country?
questions.explanation: New Zealanders are informally called 'Kiwis' after the country's iconic flightless bird.

questions.question: The fleur-de-lis, a stylized lily, is a heraldic emblem long associated with which country?
questions.explanation: The fleur-de-lis has long been a royal and heraldic symbol of France.

questions.question: The green national flag of Saudi Arabia displays the Islamic declaration of faith (the Shahada) above what other emblem?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia's flag shows the Shahada above a horizontal sword.

questions.question: The United Kingdom and Japan, where a monarch serves as ceremonial head of state under an elected government, are examples of which form of government?
questions.explanation: In a constitutional monarchy the monarch's powers are limited by a constitution and elected institutions.

questions.question: A system of government in which religious leaders rule and law is based on religious doctrine is called a:
questions.explanation: A theocracy is a state governed by religious authorities in the name of a deity.

questions.question: Government controlled by a small group of powerful people is known as a(n):
questions.explanation: An oligarchy concentrates power in the hands of a small, privileged group.

questions.question: A form of government in which political power ultimately rests with the people, exercised directly or through elected representatives, is a:
questions.explanation: In a democracy sovereignty lies with the people, who govern directly or through elected representatives.

questions.question: A state ruled by a king or queen who typically inherits the throne is a:
questions.explanation: A monarchy is headed by a king or queen, usually through hereditary succession.

questions.question: A country in which the head of state is an elected or appointed official rather than a hereditary monarch is a:
questions.explanation: A republic has a head of state chosen by election or appointment rather than by inheritance.

questions.question: A system in which sovereignty is constitutionally divided between a central authority and self-governing regional units (as in the U.S. and Germany) is a:
questions.explanation: A federation divides constitutional power between a central government and constituent regions.

questions.question: Which country is a well-known example of an absolute monarchy, where the king holds nearly all governmental power?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy in which the king exercises sweeping powers.

questions.question: A government in which power is held by the wealthy, or in which wealth is the basis of rule, is called a:
questions.explanation: A plutocracy is rule by the wealthy or a system dominated by the rich.

questions.question: Rule by a privileged hereditary class of nobility is traditionally termed:
questions.explanation: An aristocracy is government by a hereditary noble class.

questions.question: In a typical parliamentary system, the head of government usually holds which title?
questions.explanation: In most parliamentary systems the head of government is the prime minister.

questions.question: A defining feature of a presidential system such as that of the United States is that the president serves as:
options: Head of government only, with a separate head of state
A ceremonial figure with no executive power
Both head of state and head of government
questions.explanation: In a presidential system the president is simultaneously head of state and head of government.

questions.question: Vatican City is governed as which form of state, with the Pope holding supreme legislative, executive, and judicial authority?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is an absolute elective monarchy in which the elected Pope holds supreme power.

questions.question: The condition of a society with no governing authority or organized government is called:
questions.explanation: Anarchy is the absence of any ruling authority or organized government.

questions.question: A government run by a committee of military officers, typically after seizing power in a coup, is commonly called a:
questions.explanation: A junta is a government led by a group of military leaders, often installed by a coup.

questions.question: Switzerland's executive branch is unusual in that it is headed by:
options: A seven-member council whose members rotate the presidency
questions.explanation: Switzerland is led by a seven-member Federal Council, with the presidency rotating annually.
